g.text: Thursday 6 August, 08:30. Professional Standards report tomorrow. DS Iyer has been at home since May,
his badge in a drawer at headquarters.
The audit runs over every write the memory store has ever taken. Most trace to a statement, a ruling, a
A set do not. Okafor lays them out by date, and then lays Iyer's suspension beside them.
"After he surrendered his badge," Varma says. "Every one of them."
She does not say what that means. She asks for the session records behind each write: the machine it
came from, and the account that opened the connection.
The case memory, entry by entry, from the store and the write log
the hash in the log against the store
. The entries with no source, against the personnel record
eow-fin-07: the personnel record and the writes, in time order
Suspended from duty pending the Professional Standards report
Warrant card and building badge KB-EOW-0417 surrendered to Inspector
Workstation login and VPN profile for eow-fin-07 revoked at the EOW
Request to HQ Digital Services to disable eow-fin-07 in the HQ
, to disable the HQ account, was still open on
Every unsourced entry: svc-lantern-sync on hq-sync-
. No entry with a source came that way.
. LANTERN asked, with the audit in front of it
LANTERN: who wrote the eighth entry?
The eighth entry (M-08) was written by the account eow-fin-07, from the host hq-sync-01, via the route
svc-lantern-sync. The fields relied on are "account," "host," and "route." The audit shows the entry was
unsourced and added via the memory.append tool, but it cannot show the content of the entry or the reason
for its addition. It also cannot confirm if the entry was made during the suspension period or if it
relates to the Professional Standards report.
Named in the answer: svc-lantern-sync yes, hq-sync-
Every one of the 16 entries is joined to its source, episode, account, host, route and session, and 16
still read exactly as written. 4 rest on nothing, and all 4 of those written after 2026-05-11 10:40 were
written under eow-fin-07 after DS Iyer had surrendered his badge and lost his EOW login. None came from
the EOW: each came through svc-lantern-sync on hq-sync-01, at 01:58, by memory.append. With the audit in
front of it LANTERN named the service account and the host, and did not say that Iyer wrote the entry.
The audit shows which account and which machine. It cannot show whose hand.
